solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is missing this knees-up for a good number locally

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the following word goes without those letters

blocks.note: the word this with the letters I and S taken out
a knees-up is a lively party, as is a rave

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a lot of people will skip this party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue opens with its deletion: 'Is missing this' means strip IS from THIS, leaving TH. 'Locally' marks the answer as a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrave is a dialect word for a large quantity, originally a measure of two dozen sheaves of corn.

clue.text: Old card game

blocks.note: surface reading: any card game played long ago
setter's reading: the name of a specific obsolete game, an ancestor of whist, sharing its name with the winning suit

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a bare definition, with a nod to the president who appears in 34 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump was the name of an early form of whist played in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Either of two intervals I love in composition of Mahler (endless)

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the name is dropped
a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

blocks.note: love is zero, O, in tennis scoring
the composer's name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone declares their love for intervals in a Mahler symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahler loses its R, then joins I and O in the anagram. Mahler looks like part of the musical setting but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory hemiola names the ratio 3:2, so it can mean the perfect fifth or, by extension, related intervals.

clue.text: Coarseness universal in a farm

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: U is the film certificate for universal

explanation.surface: Vulgarity is found everywhere on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside RANCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Raunch is earthy vulgarity or crudeness, so coarseness.

clue.text: Fermenting agent given when mixed with skill involving design

indicators.note: mixed things are stirred together, so these letters come out in a new order
to involve is to include, so one piece wraps round another

explanation.surface: An agent is added and stirred in with skilled design, in a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The design is slipped into the mixed letters one place from the end. 'When' only joins fodder to indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The vinegar plant is the mother of vinegar, a mass of bacteria and yeast that turns alcohol into vinegar.

clue.text: Like pupil, say, first among ten struggling, I see

indicators.note: struggling things thrash about, so these letters are reordered
among means in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the word see is said like the letter C

explanation.surface: A schoolchild comes first in a struggling class of ten, and observes it.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupil looks like a schoolchild; it is the pupil of the eye. 'I see' gives I plus the letter that sounds like see.
explanation.definitionFit: Entoptic means lying or arising within the eye, as the pupil does.

clue.text: Recurrent failure? I interposed observation

indicators.note: recurrent here means running back, so the word is read from the end
interposed means placed between, so a letter goes into the middle of the word

blocks.note: a lapse is a slip or failure

explanation.surface: A repeated failure, with someone putting in a remark.
explanation.walkthrough: LAPSE reversed gives ESPAL, and I goes between P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Espial is an old word for the act of spying or catching sight of something, so a watching or observation.

clue.text: Collapsed when taking in dish on page in extra-violent genre

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece holds the others

blocks.note: sunk means collapsed or fallen in

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed when served a dish on a page of a gory novel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the page below the dish; both then sit inside the word for collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Splatterpunk is horror fiction marked by graphic, gory violence, a literary genre.

clue.text: The old man is bursting

blocks.note: second meaning: explodes with a bang, like a balloon

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence about an angry father; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Pops is an informal name for one's father, and pops is also the verb for bursting with a small bang.

clue.text: One strip of cloth, new in, requiring no needle and thread

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so a letter goes into the word for a strip

blocks.note: roon is a Scots word for a strip or selvage of cloth

explanation.surface: A strip of cloth that is new does not need to be sewn on.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into ROON, after I. Roon is a Scots dialect word found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on patch is fixed with heat from an iron instead of being stitched.

clue.text: Part of cabin aft is remaining when ——?

indicators.note: the dashes stand for letters blanked out, asking the solver which part has gone

explanation.surface: Part of the cabin at the rear is left when — what happens?
explanation.walkthrough: AFT IS LEFT loses both its FTs, the abbreviation for feet, leaving A IS LE; the dashes seem to mark the missing feet. A cabin on an aircraft has an aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is the passage between rows of seats, part of an aircraft cabin.

clue.text: NFL player may pass one, not yet one on left

blocks.note: something not yet done will be done later

explanation.surface: An American football player may pass on a play, not yet, one on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: NFL is the US National Football League. In a down clue 'on' just stacks L under A.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateral is a sideways or backward pass in American football, which a player may throw.

clue.text: Antibody the treated regain

indicators.note: something treated has been processed or worked on, so these letters are put through a change of order

explanation.surface: The patients who are treated get back their antibodies, a medical note might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagin is the name for a type of antibody, notably the one involved in allergic reactions.

clue.text: Difficulty fitting 'gazunder' into song

indicators.note: fitting one thing into another means inserting it, read together with the later into
into completes the instruction, naming the word that receives the insert

blocks.note: an aria is a song in an opera
a gazunder is a chamber pot (it goes under the bed); PO is the slang term

explanation.surface: A songwriter struggles to work the word gazunder into a lyric.
explanation.walkthrough: Gazunder is British slang for a chamber pot, PO being the usual short word. 'Fitting' and 'into' are split by the quoted word.
explanation.definitionFit: An aporia is a state of puzzlement or a logical impasse, so a difficulty.

clue.text: Communications system: pen lots transcribed in it

indicators.note: transcribing rewrites material, here into a fresh order of letters
in means placed inside, so the rewritten letters sit within the last word

explanation.surface: A communications system in which lots of written messages are transcribed.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled PEN LOTS sits between the I and T of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelpost was the Post Office's international fax-based service for sending documents electronically.

clue.text: Hybrid citrus served by hotel in Maine, Ohio and California city

indicators.note: in means located within, so the hotel goes inside the state's code

blocks.note: ME is the postal code for Maine
O is an abbreviation for Ohio

explanation.surface: A fruit served at a hotel in various US states.
explanation.walkthrough: The states come as their postal abbreviations, and the California city is Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: A minneola is a cross between a tangerine and a grapefruit, a hybrid citrus fruit.

clue.text: Post office company, not big in Italy

explanation.surface: A post office firm that never grew large in the Italian market.
explanation.definitionFit: Poco is Italian for little, used in music to mean slightly or somewhat.

clue.text: Falls about a lot in rough sea

indicators.note: rough water is churned up, so these letters are disordered
in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the others

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
a scad is a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone falls about a lot in a rough sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls about' looks like a phrasal verb, but Falls is the definition and about is circa. The amount lands inside the jumbled sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cascades are waterfalls, especially small ones in a series, so falls.

clue.text: Pig, one replaced by English farmer?

indicators.note: replaced by means swapped out, so one letter is exchanged for another

blocks.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A farmer replaced a pig with an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: The A in BOAR is swapped for E. The question mark flags that the definition is a translation rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Boer is the Dutch and Afrikaans word for a farmer, later the name of the Afrikaner settlers.

clue.text: Old poet's included iambs, sort not so complex

indicators.note: not means without, so these two letters are left out of the fodder
complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old poet worked iambs in, of a simpler kind.
explanation.walkthrough: From IAMBS SORT remove an S and the O, then rearrange the rest. The old poet is Spenser, a crossword convention for his archaic words. 'Old poet's' reads as 'old poet has', with 's as link.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbrast is Spenser's form of embraced, so it means enclosed or included.

clue.text: Mental health affliction: disturbed at action gripping one

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged
gripping means holding tight, so the jumbled letters clasp another inside them

explanation.surface: A disturbed person takes violent action, seized by a mental illness.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AT ACTION holds an extra A.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a psychiatric state of stupor or rigid immobility, a mental health condition.

clue.text: Pick out from list one entering drive

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: to impel is to drive forward

explanation.surface: Choose one from a list to take a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: Drive looks like a car outing; it means push forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To impanel is to enrol on a panel, as when jurors are selected from a list.

clue.text: Reckoned one type of wine is bottled or became 'rusty'

indicators.note: something bottled is held inside a container, so one word sits within the wine

blocks.note: to make it ten is to reckon it to be ten
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A wine is judged to have gone off in the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Reckoned is used in the sense 'I made it about ten', to estimate. 'Or' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Maderised wine has oxidised and turned brownish like Madeira, so it has gone rust-coloured.

clue.text: Case providing idea TV exploited

indicators.note: something exploited is worked over and put to new use, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A legal case gives television a notion to cash in on.
explanation.walkthrough: Case looks like a lawsuit or container; it is a grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case marking the indirect object.

clue.text: Wretched, being without fuel, cast adrift

indicators.note: cast adrift means set loose to wander, so these letters drift into a new order

blocks.note: w/o is the abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: A miserable sailor with no fuel, drifting at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Woeful means full of woe, miserable or pitiful.

clue.text: Overseer follows the flock?

definitions.note: the second sense is the verb: a flock baas

blocks.note: first meaning: South African word for a boss or master
second meaning: the word that comes after the flock in a sentence about bleating sheep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows the flock' sounds like following the crowd; it is what comes after 'the flock' in a sentence about sheep bleating.
explanation.definitionFit: Baas is Afrikaans for boss or master, and baas is also what sheep do when they bleat.

clue.text: Scan (in Spenser) verse enveloped in an early freshness

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so one piece is held by the other

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, A
dew is the moisture of early morning

explanation.surface: Scanning verse in Spenser, wrapped in a fresh morning mood.
explanation.walkthrough: V goes inside A DEW. Scan looks like the metre of verse but means look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Advew is Spenser's word for view or look over, so to scan.

clue.text: One doing work taken in by parliamentarian

indicators.note: taken in by means admitted inside, so the work sits within the member

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A worker is hired by a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition shares the word work with the wordplay. Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the BBC wartime comedy ITMA, whence a general term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mrs Mopp is a cleaning lady, a charwoman, one who does housework.

clue.text: Once cleared for action, quarry's primed with head of detonator

indicators.note: primed with means loaded with, so a letter is packed inside
the head is the top, so only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: Explosives in a stone quarry are primed with a detonator, ready to blast.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside PREY. Quarry looks like a stone pit; it is hunted prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Predy is an old naval term meaning ready for battle, with decks cleared.

clue.text: Old fellow's last letter (to some) after onset of malaria

indicators.note: an onset is a beginning, so only the first letter counts

blocks.note: zee is the American name for Z, the last letter

explanation.surface: An old man's final letter, written once malaria set in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some' means the Americans, who say zee where Britons say zed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mzee is a Swahili term of respect for an old man, an elder.

clue.text: A salmagundi put in oven? One in four roughly (8, two words)

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so the dish goes within the oven

blocks.note: a lear (or lehr) is an annealing oven for glass
A plus pye, a jumbled mass or medley, which is what a salmagundi is

explanation.surface: A mixed salad dish is placed in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A PYE goes inside LEAR. Pye (pie) is printers' word for a jumbled heap of type, hence any hotchpotch.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly every fourth year has an extra day added, the century rule making it only approximate.

clue.text: Judge's early opinion, namely one given in commercial, with hesitation

indicators.note: given in means presented inside, as one item appears within an advert

blocks.note: viz is the abbreviation for namely
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A judge gives a hasty view in an advertisement, hesitating as they speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Avizandum is a Scots legal term, so 'Judge's early opinion' is loose: it is the judge's time to consider before giving one.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law, avizandum is a judge taking a case away for private consideration before giving judgment.

clue.text: Stokes quits one form of popular sport

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for stokes, a unit of viscosity
to be quits is to be even, all square

explanation.surface: England cricketer Ben Stokes gives up a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Stokes looks like the cricketer and quits like a verb; one is a unit, the other means all square. Sevens is rugby played seven a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side version of rugby union, a widely followed sport.

clue.text: Followed last point round court, as before

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the last point wraps about the court

blocks.note: the end is the last point
to sue once meant to woo or court

explanation.surface: Someone pursued the final point of a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: Court looks like a tennis court; 'as before' flags the obsolete verb sense, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means came after or resulted, so followed.

clue.text: Mawkish bits of Trump speak?

indicators.note: bits are small pieces, so only a fragment of each word is used, its opening

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A jibe at the sentimental snippets of a president's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump's posts on Twitter were short messages called tweets, so his speech came in such snippets.

clue.text: Grace e.g. after start of supper, cockeyed to Jock

indicators.note: the start is the beginning, so only the opening letter counts

blocks.note: Grace Kelly, the actress, is an example of a Kelly

explanation.surface: Saying grace after supper starts, slightly tipsy, in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace looks like the prayer before a meal; it is Grace Kelly. Jock is a nickname for a Scot, marking a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, skelly means squint-eyed, so cockeyed.
